This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: pom.xml
- runtime entry: src/main/java/Main.java
- single test target: src/test/java/MainTest.java
- test command: mvn -q test
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use Maven and Java 11 without preview features. Main.java must be in the default package because the evaluator runs Main. Put every other project class directly under src/main/java and keep it in the default package too; do not create package subdirectories or package declarations. This deliberately avoids package/import mismatches in independently generated files. Keep core logic independent from Swing/JavaFX; prefer no GUI and no non-test external dependency. pom.xml MUST declare org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter with test scope and a Maven Surefire version that runs JUnit 5; MainTest.java must use JUnit Jupiter only. Repeat this exact dependency contract in the pom.xml task.

Medium-size reference from MetaProjectDev (descriptive only; the architecture model's generated file count is authoritative):
- about 7 repository files
- about 31 functions or methods
- about 590 lines of code

Sizing guidance:
- #Files, #Functions, and #LOC above are paper-table references, not acceptance bounds
- use the number of files produced by this architecture run; do not add or remove files merely to hit the reference
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files when reporting the realized size

Required domain behavior:
- grid-based snake movement
- direction rules that reject immediate reversal
- food placement and consumption
- growth and score updates
- wall and self collision
- game-over and reset

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- keep the single test target concise (2 to 4 tests, preferably under 150 LOC): cover runtime wiring and representative core rules, not the full feature matrix
- do not inflate the function/LOC target with test code; put substantive behavior in implementation files
- make every planned file small enough for one 4096-token code completion: prefer under 150 LOC and never plan a file over 220 LOC
- order the Task list strictly by implementation dependency: foundational types and interfaces first, then dependent implementations, then the runtime entry, and the single test target LAST (the build descriptor may be first)
- the Engineer code_todos must preserve that dependency-first Task-list order so later files can see already-generated dependency code
- the runtime entry must provide a small non-interactive demonstration that exits successfully or starts safely without an output loop
- validate invalid inputs and boundary cases
- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- specify one canonical public API; tests must use it without inventing alternate semantics
- make Full API spec non-empty and exhaustive: for every public type/function give its exact module, signature, return value, error behavior, and key semantics; repeat these exact contracts in each affected file task
- tests may import only the canonical public API and should assert stable externally visible behavior, not private implementation details, incidental formatting, or unplanned aliases
- avoid circular dependencies; explicitly give the allowed import/include direction and ensure every referenced symbol is defined before a dependent file is generated
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents

Generate a complete medium-size Java 11 repository architecture for: Snake game.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: pom.xml
- runtime entry: src/main/java/Main.java
- single test target: src/test/java/MainTest.java
- test command: mvn -q test
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use Maven and Java 11 without preview features. Main.java must be in the default package because the evaluator runs Main. Put every other project class directly under src/main/java and keep it in the default package too; do not create package subdirectories or package declarations. This deliberately avoids package/import mismatches in independently generated files. Keep core logic independent from Swing/JavaFX; prefer no GUI and no non-test external dependency. pom.xml MUST declare org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter with test scope and a Maven Surefire version that runs JUnit 5; MainTest.java must use JUnit Jupiter only. Repeat this exact dependency contract in the pom.xml task.

Medium-size reference from MetaProjectDev (descriptive only; the architecture model's generated file count is authoritative):
- about 7 repository files
- about 31 functions or methods
- about 590 lines of code

Sizing guidance:
- #Files, #Functions, and #LOC above are paper-table references, not acceptance bounds
- use the number of files produced by this architecture run; do not add or remove files merely to hit the reference
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files when reporting the realized size

Required domain behavior:
- grid-based snake movement
- direction rules that reject immediate reversal
- food placement and consumption
- growth and score updates
- wall and self collision
- game-over and reset

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- keep the single test target concise (2 to 4 tests, preferably under 150 LOC): cover runtime wiring and representative core rules, not the full feature matrix
- do not inflate the function/LOC target with test code; put substantive behavior in implementation files
- make every planned file small enough for one 4096-token code completion: prefer under 150 LOC and never plan a file over 220 LOC
- order the Task list strictly by implementation dependency: foundational types and interfaces first, then dependent implementations, then the runtime entry, and the single test target LAST (the build descriptor may be first)
- the Engineer code_todos must preserve that dependency-first Task-list order so later files can see already-generated dependency code
- the runtime entry must provide a small non-interactive demonstration that exits successfully or starts safely without an output loop
- validate invalid inputs and boundary cases
- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- specify one canonical public API; tests must use it without inventing alternate semantics
- make Full API spec non-empty and exhaustive: for every public type/function give its exact module, signature, return value, error behavior, and key semantics; repeat these exact contracts in each affected file task
- tests may import only the canonical public API and should assert stable externally visible behavior, not private implementation details, incidental formatting, or unplanned aliases
- avoid circular dependencies; explicitly give the allowed import/include direction and ensure every referenced symbol is defined before a dependent file is generated
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents

  - public Direction getDirection(): current movement direction.
  - public MoveOutcome tick(): advances exactly one cell by current direction. If next head is food, grows snake, increments score by 1, places new food randomly among free cells; returns ATE_FOOD. If next head is out-of-bounds or collides with the body, sets gameOver=true and returns GAME_OVER. Otherwise moves normally and returns MOVED. If the board is full after eating (no free cells), sets gameOver=true.
  - public boolean isGameOver()
  - public int getScore()
  - public int getWidth()
  - public int getHeight()
  - public GameSnapshot snapshot(): returns an immutable snapshot of current state.
  - public void placeFoodAt(Position p): deterministically place food at p after validating bounds and that p is not occupied by the snake; useful for tests.
- Helper (non-public) methods:
  - private void placeFoodRandomly(): choose uniformly among free cells using rng.nextInt(bound) where bound equals count of free cells.
  - private boolean inBounds(Position p): 0 <= x < width and 0 <= y < height.
- Errors: Constructor and reset validate width>0 and height>0; throw IllegalArgumentException otherwise. placeFoodAt throws IllegalArgumentException for out-of-bounds or occupied cells. tick on gameOver leaves state unchanged and returns GAME_OVER.
- Grid: origin top-left; x increases to the right, y increases downward.

Main (src/main/java/Main.java)
- public final class Main
- Methods:
  - public static void main(String[] args): creates JavaUtilRandomSource with a fixed seed, constructs SnakeGame with a small grid, prints initial snapshot, performs a few deterministic ticks printing MoveOutcome and final snapshot, catches any Exception by printing a single line and exiting normally (no rethrow).

Import direction rules
- Core domain (Position, Direction, MoveOutcome, Snake, GameSnapshot, SnakeGame, RandomSource) must not import environment-dependent classes.
- Environment-dependent (Main, JavaUtilRandomSource) may depend on core domain.
- Tests import and exercise only the canonical API and may define in-test stubs for RandomSource.

places food randomly.\\n  - public boolean setDirection(Direction dir): sets intended movement direction if dir is non-null and not an immediate reversal of current direction; returns true if accepted, false if rejected.\\n  - public Direction getDirection(): current movement direction.\\n  - public MoveOutcome tick(): advances exactly one cell by current direction. If next head is food, grows snake, increments score by 1, places new food randomly among free cells; returns ATE_FOOD. If next head is out-of-bounds or collides with the body, sets gameOver=true and returns GAME_OVER. Otherwise moves normally and returns MOVED. Contract: bound must be > 0; implementors may throw IllegalArgumentException for invalid bound.\\n\\nJavaUtilRandomSource (src/main/java/JavaUtilRandomSource.java)\\n- public final class JavaUtilRandomSource implements RandomSource\\n- Constructors:\\n  - public JavaUtilRandomSource(long seed): deterministic for a given seed.\\n- Methods:\\n  - public int nextInt(int bound): delegates to java.util.Random, validating bound > 0; must not reflect future state changes.\\n\\nSnakeGame (src/main/java/SnakeGame.java)\\n- public final class SnakeGame\\n- Constructors:\\n  - public SnakeGame(int width, int height, RandomSource rng): initializes a new game with the snake at a valid starting cell, score=0, gameOver=false, initial direction (implementation-defined but consistent), and a randomly placed food on a free cell using rng.\\n- Methods:\\n  - public void reset(): resets to a fresh game state using the same width, height, and rng; places food randomly.\\n  - public boolean setDirection(Direction dir): sets intended movement direction if dir is non-null and not an immediate reversal of current direction; returns true if accepted, false if rejected.\\n  - public Direction getDirection(): current movement direction.\\n  - public MoveOutcome tick(): advances exactly one cell by current direction. If next head is food, grows snake, increments score by 1, places new food randomly among free cells; returns ATE_FOOD. If next head is out-of-bounds or collides with the body, sets gameOver=true and returns GAME_OVER. Otherwise moves normally and returns MOVED. If the board is full after eating (no free cells), sets gameOver=true.\\n  - public boolean isGameOver()\\n  - public int getScore()\\n  - public int getWidth()\\n  - public int getHeight()\\n  - public GameSnapshot snapshot(): returns an immutable snapshot of current state.\\n  - public void placeFoodAt(Position p): deterministically place food at p after validating bounds and that p is not occupied by the snake; useful for tests.\\n- Helper (non-public) methods:\\n  - private void placeFoodRandomly(): choose uniformly among free cells using rng.nextInt(bound) where bound equals count of free cells.\\n  - private boolean inBounds(Position p): 0 <= x < width and 0 <= y < height.\\n- Errors: Constructor and reset validate width>0 and height>0; throw IllegalArgumentException otherwise. placeFoodAt throws IllegalArgumentException for out-of-bounds or occupied cells. tick on gameOver leaves state unchanged and returns GAME_OVER.\\n- Grid: origin top-left; x increases to the right, y increases downward.\\n\\nMain (src/main/java/Main.java)\\n- public final class Main\\n- Methods:\\n  - public static void main(String[] args): creates JavaUtilRandomSource with a fixed seed, constructs SnakeGame with a small grid, prints initial snapshot, performs a few deterministic ticks printing MoveOutcome and final snapshot, catches any Exception by printing a single line and exiting normally (no rethrow).\\n\\nImport direction rules\\n- Core domain (Position, Direction, MoveOutcome, Snake, GameSnapshot, SnakeGame, RandomSource) must not import environment-dependent classes.\\n- Environment-dependent (Main, JavaUtilRandomSource) may depend on core domain.\\n- Tests import and exercise only the canonical API and may define in-test stubs for RandomSource.\\n\",\"Shared Knowledge\":\"Project is a Maven Java 11 application. Contract: bound must be > 0; implementors may throw IllegalArgumentException for invalid bound.\\n\\nJavaUtilRandomSource (src/main/java/JavaUtilRandomSource.java)\\n- public final class JavaUtilRandomSource implements RandomSource\\n- Constructors:\\n  - public JavaUtilRandomSource(long seed): deterministic for a given seed.\\n- Methods:\\n  - public int nextInt(int bound): delegates to java.util.Random, validating bound > 0; throws IllegalArgumentException if bound <= 0.\\n\\nMoveOutcome (src/main/java/MoveOutcome.java)\\n- public enum MoveOutcome { MOVED, ATE_FOOD, GAME_OVER }\\n- Semantics: result classification for a single tick.\\n\\nSnake (src/main/java/Snake.java)\\n- public final class Snake\\n- Constructors:\\n  - public Snake(Position start): creates a snake with a single-segment body at start.\\n- Methods:\\n  - public Position head(): returns current head position.\\n  - public Position tail(): returns current tail position.\\n  - public int length(): number of segments.\\n  - public boolean occupies(Position p): true if any segment equals p.\\n  - public void moveTo(Position nextHead): adds nextHead at head and removes the last tail segment.\\n  - public void growTo(Position nextHead): adds nextHead at head and retains tail (length+1).\\n  - public java.util.List<Position> bodyAsList(): returns a defensive immutable/copy list of body positions in head-to-tail order.\\n- Errors: Public methods validate non-null inputs and throw NullPointerException or IllegalArgumentException as appropriate.\\n\\nGameSnapshot (src/main/java/GameSnapshot.java)\\n- public final class GameSnapshot\\n- Constructors:\\n  - public GameSnapshot(int width, int height, java.util.List<Position> body, Position food, int score, boolean gameOver, Direction direction)\\n- Methods:\\n  - public int getWidth()\\n  - public int getHeight()\\n  - public java.util.List<Position> getSnakeBody(): returns an unmodifiable copy/view.\\n  - public Position getFood()\\n  - public int getScore()\\n  - public boolean isGameOver()\\n  - public Direction getDirection()\\n  - public String toString(): concise summary for debugging/logging.\\n- Semantics: immutable snapshot suitable for observers/tests; must not reflect future state changes.\\n\\nSnakeGame (src/main/java/SnakeGame.java)\\n- public final class SnakeGame\\n- Constructors:\\n  - public SnakeGame(int width, int height, RandomSource rng): initializes a new game with the snake at a valid starting cell, score=0, gameOver=false, initial direction (implementation-defined but consistent), and a randomly placed food on a free cell using rng.\\n- Methods:\\n  - public void reset(): resets to a fresh game state using the same width, height, and rng; places food randomly.\\n  - public boolean setDirection(Direction dir): sets intended movement direction if dir is non-null and not an immediate reversal of current direction; returns true if accepted, false if rejected.\\n  - public Direction getDirection(): current movement direction.\\n  - public MoveOutcome tick(): advances exactly one cell by current direction. If next head is food, grows snake, increments score by 1, places new food randomly among free cells; returns ATE_FOOD. If next head is out-of-bounds or collides with the body, sets gameOver=true and returns GAME_OVER. Otherwise moves normally and returns MOVED. If the board is full after eating (no free cells), sets gameOver=true.\\n  - public boolean isGameOver()\\n  - public int getScore()\\n  - public int getWidth()\\n  - public int getHeight()\\n  - public GameSnapshot snapshot(): returns an immutable snapshot of current state.\\n  - public void placeFoodAt(Position p): deterministically place food at p after validating bounds and that p is not occupied by the snake; useful for tests.\\n- Helper (non-public) methods:\\n  - private void placeFoodRandomly(): choose uniformly among free cells using rng.nextInt(bound) where bound equals count of free cells.\\n  - private boolean inBounds(Position p): 0 <= x < width and 0 <= y < height.\\n- Errors: Constructor and reset validate width>0 and height>0; throw IllegalArgumentException otherwise. placeFoodAt throws IllegalArgumentException for out-of-bounds or occupied cells. tick on gameOver leaves state unchanged and returns GAME_OVER.\\n- Grid: origin top-left; x increases to the right, y increases downward.\\n\\nMain (src/main/java/Main.java)\\n- public final class Main\\n- Methods:\\n  - public static void main(String[] args): creates JavaUtilRandomSource with a fixed seed, constructs SnakeGame with a small grid, prints initial snapshot, performs a few deterministic ticks printing MoveOutcome and final snapshot, catches any Exception by printing a single line and exiting normally (no rethrow).\\n\\nImport direction rules\\n- Core domain (Position, Direction, MoveOutcome, Snake, GameSnapshot, SnakeGame, RandomSource) must not import environment-dependent classes.\\n- Environment-dependent (Main, JavaUtilRandomSource) may depend on core domain.\\n- Tests import and exercise only the canonical API and may define in-test stubs for RandomSource.\\n\",\"Shared Knowledge\":\"Project is a Maven Java 11 application. Generate a complete medium-size Java 11 repository architecture for: Snake game.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: pom.xml
- runtime entry: src/main/java/Main.java
- single test target: src/test/java/MainTest.java
- test command: mvn -q test
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use Maven and Java 11 without preview features. Main.java must be in the default package because the evaluator runs Main. Put every other project class directly under src/main/java and keep it in the default package too; do not create package subdirectories or package declarations. This deliberately avoids package/import mismatches in independently generated files. Keep core logic independent from Swing/JavaFX; prefer no GUI and no non-test external dependency. pom.xml MUST declare org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter with test scope and a Maven Surefire version that runs JUnit 5; MainTest.java must use JUnit Jupiter only. Repeat this exact dependency contract in the pom.xml task.

Medium-size reference from MetaProjectDev (descriptive only; the architecture model's generated file count is authoritative):
- about 7 repository files
- about 31 functions or methods
- about 590 lines of code

Sizing guidance:
- #Files, #Functions, and #LOC above are paper-table references, not acceptance bounds
- use the number of files produced by this architecture run; do not add or remove files merely to hit the reference
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files when reporting the realized size

Required domain behavior:
- grid-based snake movement
- direction rules that reject immediate reversal
- food placement and consumption
- growth and score updates
- wall and self collision
- game-over and reset

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- keep the single test target concise (2 to 4 tests, preferably under 150 LOC): cover runtime wiring and representative core rules, not the full feature matrix
- do not inflate the function/LOC target with test code; put substantive behavior in implementation files
- make every planned file small enough for one 4096-token code completion: prefer under 150 LOC and never plan a file over 220 LOC
- order the Task list strictly by implementation dependency: foundational types and interfaces first, then dependent implementations, then the runtime entry, and the single test target LAST (the build descriptor may be first)
- the Engineer code_todos must preserve that dependency-first Task-list order so later files can see already-generated dependency code
- the runtime entry must provide a small non-interactive demonstration that exits successfully or starts safely without an output loop
- validate invalid inputs and boundary cases
- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- specify one canonical public API; tests must use it without inventing alternate semantics
- make Full API spec non-empty and exhaustive: for every public type/function give its exact module, signature, return value, error behavior, and key semantics; repeat these exact contracts in each affected file task
- tests may import only the canonical public API and should assert stable externally visible behavior, not private implementation details, incidental formatting, or unplanned aliases
- avoid circular dependencies; explicitly give the allowed import/include direction and ensure every referenced symbol is defined before a dependent file is generated
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents

- Constructors:
  - public Snake(Position start): creates a snake with a single-segment body at start.
- Methods:
  - public Position head(): returns current head position.
  - public Position tail(): returns current tail position.
  - public int length(): number of segments.
  - public boolean occupies(Position p): true if any segment equals p.
  - public void moveTo(Position nextHead): adds nextHead at head and removes the last tail segment.
  - public void growTo(Position nextHead): adds nextHead at head and retains tail (length+1).
  - public java.util.List<Position> bodyAsList(): returns a defensive immutable/copy list of body positions in head-to-tail order.
- Errors: Public methods validate non-null inputs and throw NullPointerException or IllegalArgumentException as appropriate.

GameSnapshot (src/main/java/GameSnapshot.java)
- public final class GameSnapshot
- Constructors:
  - public GameSnapshot(int width, int height, java.util.List<Position> body, Position food, int score, boolean gameOver, Direction direction)
- Methods:
  - public int getWidth()
  - public int getHeight()
  - public java.util.List<Position> getSnakeBody(): returns an unmodifiable copy/view.
  - public Position getFood()
  - public int getScore()
  - public boolean isGameOver()
  - public Direction getDirection()
  - public String toString(): concise summary for debugging/logging.
- Semantics: immutable snapshot suitable for observers/tests; must not reflect future state changes.

SnakeGame (src/main/java/SnakeGame.java)
- public final class SnakeGame
- Constructors:
  - public SnakeGame(int width, int height, RandomSource rng): initializes a new game with the snake at a valid starting cell, score=0, gameOver=false, initial direction (implementation-defined but consistent), and a randomly placed food on a free cell using rng.
- Methods:
  - public void reset(): resets to a fresh game state using the same width, height, and rng; places food randomly.
  - public boolean setDirection(Direction dir): sets intended movement direction if dir is non-null and not an immediate reversal of current direction; returns true if accepted, false if rejected.
  - public Direction getDirection(): current movement direction.
  - public MoveOutcome tick(): advances exactly one cell by current direction. If next head is food, grows snake, increments score by 1, places new food randomly among free cells; returns ATE_FOOD. If next head is out-of-bounds or collides with the body, sets gameOver=true and returns GAME_OVER. Otherwise moves normally and returns MOVED. If the board is full after eating (no free cells), sets gameOver=true.
  - public boolean isGameOver()
  - public int getScore()
  - public int getWidth()
  - public int getHeight()
  - public GameSnapshot snapshot(): returns an immutable snapshot of current state.
  - public void placeFoodAt(Position p): deterministically place food at p after validating bounds and that p is not occupied by the snake; useful for tests.
- Helper (non-public) methods:
  - private void placeFoodRandomly(): choose uniformly among free cells using rng.nextInt(bound) where bound equals count of free cells.
  - private boolean inBounds(Position p): 0 <= x < width and 0 <= y < height.
- Errors: Constructor and reset validate width>0 and height>0; throw IllegalArgumentException otherwise. placeFoodAt throws IllegalArgumentException for out-of-bounds or occupied cells. tick on gameOver leaves state unchanged and returns GAME_OVER.
- Grid: origin top-left; x increases to the right, y increases downward.

Main (src/main/java/Main.java)
- public final class Main
- Methods:
  - public static void main(String[] args): creates JavaUtilRandomSource with a fixed seed, constructs SnakeGame with a small grid, prints initial snapshot, performs a few deterministic ticks printing MoveOutcome and final snapshot, catches any Exception by printing a single line and exiting normally (no rethrow).

Import direction rules
- Core domain (Position, Direction, MoveOutcome, Snake, GameSnapshot, SnakeGame, RandomSource) must not import environment-dependent classes.
- Environment-dependent (Main, JavaUtilRandomSource) may depend on core domain.
- Tests import and exercise only the canonical API and may define in-test stubs for RandomSource.

- test command: mvn -q test

Language/layout constraints:
Use Maven and Java 11 without preview features. Main.java must be in the default package because the evaluator runs Main. Put every other project class directly under src/main/java and keep it in the default package too; do not create package subdirectories or package declarations. This deliberately avoids package/import mismatches in independently generated files. Keep core logic independent from Swing/JavaFX; prefer no GUI and no non-test external dependency. pom.xml MUST declare org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter with test scope and a Maven Surefire version that runs JUnit 5; MainTest.java must use JUnit Jupiter only. Repeat this exact dependency contract in the pom.xml task.

Medium-size reference from MetaProjectDev (descriptive only; the architecture model's generated file count is authoritative):
- about 7 repository files
- about 31 functions or methods
- about 590 lines of code

- #Files, #Functions, and #LOC above are paper-table references, not acceptance bounds
- use the number of files produced by this architecture run; do not add or remove files merely to hit the reference
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files when reporting the realized size

Required domain behavior:
- grid-based snake movement
- direction rules that reject immediate reversal
- food placement and consumption
- growth and score updates
- wall and self collision
- game-over and reset

- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction

- the runtime entry must provide a small non-interactive demonstration that exits successfully or starts safely without an output loop
- validate invalid inputs and boundary cases
- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- specify one canonical public API; tests must use it without inventing alternate semantics
- make Full API spec non-empty and exhaustive: for every public type/function give its exact module, signature, return value, error behavior, and key semantics; repeat these exact contracts in each affected file task
- tests may import only the canonical public API and should assert stable externally visible behavior, not private implementation details, incidental formatting, or unplanned aliases
- avoid circular dependencies; explicitly give the allowed import/include direction and ensure every referenced symbol is defined before a dependent file is generated
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents
